newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: PRESS DIGEST - Australian Business News - June 19.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Australian Business News - June 19.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

The merger of South African minerals company Gencor's nickel assets with Australia's dominant refiner Queensland Nickel will create a A$2.3 billion nickel mining and refining giant. This will account for over seven per cent of international production an be one of the four biggest nickel producers in the world. Page 1.

New figure compiled by Japan's Ministry of Finance show Japan is turning its back on Australia as a place for investment as investments in other parts of the world are booming. The figures reveal Japanese foreign direct investment in Australia fell to A$1 billion in the 12 months to March 1997, the lowest level in 10 years. Page 1.

Struggling with tightened financial circumstances after its merger with pay-TV and local telephony offshoot Optus Vision Ltd, Optus Communications Ltd faces two options: call on shareholders to bring in extra capital ahead of its sharemarket float, or raise more than its planned A$400 million to A$500 million from its public share sale. Page 21.

Following its debut on the Australian Stock Exchange four weeks ago, Colonial Ltd's shares have risen a further 11 cents to A$3.50, prompting a push by institutional investors to build their shareholding to index weighting. Several institutions are yet to build up their shares thanks to a high retention of shares by policyholders. Page 21.

Following overwhelming support by shareholders for the merger of Kingstream Resources and Taiwan's An Feng Steel Co, the two companies now plan to raise A$673 million of new equity and A$1 billion of debt to set the ball rolling in Western Australia's MidWest steel project. Page 22.

Perth-based miner Australian Gold Fields NL yesterday finalised the A$20.28 million purchase of Hidden Valley Gold Pty Ltd from Rio Tinto Ltd, and will now consolidate the Hidden Valley project with the nearby Wau gold project to form a combined resource of 5.6 million ounces of gold in the Morobe province of Papua New Guinea. Page 22.
THE AUSTRALIAN

A partnership of BHP with Royal Dutch/Shell Canada will see the development of the A$960 million Lease 13 oil sands project in Alberta, Canada. BHP Minerals will have a 25 per cent stake in the first stage of the project, which will involve a study of a reserve estimated to contain five billion barrels of bitumen. Page 21.

Under a A$2.3 billion proposal to establish the world's fourth largest nickel producer, South African mining giant Gencor will take a 55 per cent controlling share of nickel refiner QNI. The deal is part of a broader strategy for Gencor to provide its asset base with access to the international capital markets. Page 21.

A multi-million out-of-court settlement offer from ICI Australia has been rejected by farmers who are suing the company over contamination of their cattle herds by ICI's Helix cotton pesticide, which was on the market from 1989 to 1994. A vote against the settlement by 400 farmers in Narrabri yesterday will see the case return to the Federal Court in Sydney for judgement. Page 21.

WMC chairman Sir Arvi Parbo has told a Brisbane dinner the company's A$650 million Phosphate Hill fertiliser project near Mt Isa could double its output to about two million tonnes a year following strong interest from Asian buyers. Parbo said the initial returns of one million a year will satisfy more than half of the Australian market as well as some export demand. Page 22.

The release of further drilling results from Carpenter Pacific's Mt Kare gold project in Papua New Guinea have revealed further gold intersections and backed up results issued in April showing high-grade gold in 10 drill holes. The results indicate the controversial mine could be in the same league as the nearby Porgera project. Page 22.

The Australian Competition and Consumer Commission's draft pricing structure for access to the Telstra network after deregulation in July, which proposes a 40 per cent cut in interconnection rates, has been supported by telecommunications service provider. Page 23.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

In a move designed to revamp its operations and cut costs, the ANZ Banking Group will change from its geographic reporting management system to a product-based structure. The new structure may partly explain the early retirement of ANZ's executive director, international, Alister Maitland, as it appears he was left without a position. Page 29.

Westpac Banking Corp, ANZ, National Australia Bank, Citibank and GE Capital are among the possible bidders for Ansett Australia's 68 per cent stake in Diners Club (Australia), which would sell for around A$43 million. The move is part of Ansett's strategy to focus on its core aviation business. Page 29.

QNI yesterday confirmed a deal which will see 504.3 million QNI shares issued to South African mining company Gencor, giving Gencor a 56 per cent share of QNI and providing it with a platform to become a major player in the world nickel industry. Page 29.

Financial advisers to WA steel project Kingstream Resources said yesterday the group would wade into equity markets over the next few months in a bid to raise about $670 million. The company plans to borrow a further $1.1 billion to commence the project. Page 31.

The Reserve Bank may have to raise interest rates in response to wage pressures and weak export demand despite the persistent weak activity shown in the latest Westpac-Melbourne Institute that demands lower rates. The OECD conceded employment would be higher in 1998 than the Government has forecast, and Australia was yet to see a reward from labour market reforms. Page 31.

The home loan interest rate battle strengthened yesterday with Westpac Banking Corp and HongkongBank Australia lowering their fixed home loan rates by up to 0.5 percentage points, joining other banks in an effort to encourage borrowers to lock in at low interest rates to protect against any future increases in official rates. Page 31.
THE AGE

QNI will hand over its control to South African mining giant Gencor in a A$2.3 billion deal that will see the two companies gain the solidity and size required to compete for market attention with the world's major nickel producers. The deal will see QNI acquire Gencor's nickel assets and will give the company a 56 per cent controlling stake. Page C1.

Following recommendations from international consulting firm KPMG Barents, the ANZ Bank will replace its current management system of geographic reporting lines with a product-based structure. Page C1.

A spokesperson from the Australian Competition and Consumer Commission says the regulator is set to report on the A$1.4 billion merger between Westpac and the Bank of Melbourne Ltd towards the end of this month. Analysts believe the merger will be approved. Page C1.

Shares in Southern Pacific Petroleum and Central Pacific Minerals were placed with international institutions yesterday, bringing the Stuart shale oil project, near Gladstone in Queensland, closer to reality. The placement is yet to be finalised but there are indications that demand will exceed expectations and raise close to A$90 million. Page C3.

A joint A$971 million oil sands project between Shell Canada and BHP Minerals, titled Lease 13, is in the pre-feasibility study phase, with BHP Minerals exposure limited to 25 per cent of costs at this stage. The project has the potential to produce 120,00 to 150,000 barrels of bitumen a day. Page C3.

Westpac has cut its one-year guaranteed home loan rate to 6.49 per cent, with a spokesman saying the cuts were achievable because of the fall in the cost of the bank's funds. The lowering of fixed home-loan rates will see competition in the sector increase. Page C3.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
